The development of BLAKE3 was sponsored by [Electric Coin Company](https://electriccoin.co). *NOTE: BLAKE3 is not a password hashing algorithm, because it's designed to be fast, whereas password hashing should not be fast. If you hash passwords to store the hashes or if you derive keys from passwords, we recommend [Argon2](https://github.com/P-H-C/phc-winner-argon2).* ## The `b3sum` Command Line Tool The `b3sum` command line utility prints the BLAKE3 hashes of files or of standard input. ### Usage ``` Usage: b3sum [OPTIONS] [FILE]... Arguments: [FILE]... Files to hash, or checkfiles to check Options: --keyed Use the keyed mode, reading the 32-byte key from stdin --derive-key Use the key derivation mode, with the given context string -l, --length The number of output bytes, before hex encoding [default: 32] --seek The starting output byte offset, before hex encoding [default: 0] --num-threads The maximum number of threads to use --no-mmap Disable memory mapping --no-names Omit filenames in the output --raw Write raw output bytes to stdout, rather than hex --tag Output BSD-style checksums: BLAKE3 ([FILE]) = [HASH] -c, --check Read BLAKE3 sums from the [FILE]s and check them --quiet Skip printing OK for each checked file -h, --help Print help (see more with '--help') -V, --version Print version ``` ### Examples Hash a file: ```bash b3sum foo.txt ``` Hash multiple files: ```bash b3sum file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt ``` Hash from standard input: ```bash echo "hello world" | b3sum ``` Check hashes from a checksum file: ```bash b3sum -c checksums.txt ``` Generate a longer hash output (e.g., 64 bytes): ```bash b3sum --length 64 foo.txt ``` Use keyed hashing mode: ```bash echo "my secret key padded to 32 bytes" | b3sum --keyed foo.txt ``` Use key derivation mode: ```bash b3sum --derive-key "my-app 2024-01-01 user-id" < input_key_material.bin ``` ### Installation Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, Windows, and macOS on the [releases page](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/releases). ## BLAKE3 Library Usage BLAKE3 is available as a library for multiple programming languages. ### Rust To use BLAKE3 from Rust code, add a dependency on the `blake3` crate: ```rust // Hash an input all at once. let hash1 = blake3::hash(b"foobarbaz"); // Hash an input incrementally. let mut hasher = blake3::Hasher::new(); hasher.update(b"foo"); hasher.update(b"bar"); hasher.update(b"baz"); let hash2 = hasher.finalize(); assert_eq!(hash1, hash2); // Extended output. # b3sum

A command line utility for calculating [BLAKE3](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3) hashes,
similar to Coreutils tools like `b2sum` or `md5sum`.

## Usage

```
Usage: b3sum [OPTIONS] [FILE]...

Arguments:
  [FILE]...  Files to hash, or checkfiles to check

Options:
      --keyed                 Use the keyed mode, reading the 32-byte key from stdin
      --derive-key <CONTEXT>  Use the key derivation mode, with the given context string
  -l, --length <LEN>          The number of output bytes, before hex encoding [default: 32]
      --seek <SEEK>           The starting output byte offset, before hex encoding [default: 0]
      --num-threads <NUM>     The maximum number of threads to use
      --no-mmap               Disable memory mapping
      --no-names              Omit filenames in the output
      --raw                   Write raw output bytes to stdout, rather than hex
      --tag                   Output BSD-style checksums: BLAKE3 ([FILE]) = [HASH]
  -c, --check                 Read BLAKE3 sums from the [FILE]s and check them
      --quiet                 Skip printing OK for each checked file
  -h, --help                  Print help (see more with '--help')
  -V, --version               Print version
```

## Examples

Hash a file:

```bash
b3sum foo.txt
```

Hash multiple files:

```bash
b3sum file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt
```

Hash from standard input:

```bash
echo "hello world" | b3sum
```

Time hashing a large file to see performance:

```bash
# Create a 1 GB file
head -c 1000000000 /dev/zero > /tmp/bigfile
# Hash it with SHA-256
time openssl sha256 /tmp/bigfile
# Hash it with BLAKE3 (notice the speed difference!)
time b3sum /tmp/bigfile
```

Check hashes from a checksum file:

```bash
b3sum -c checksums.txt
```

Generate a longer hash output (e.g., 64 bytes):

```bash
b3sum --length 64 foo.txt
```

Use keyed hashing mode (for message authentication):

```bash
echo "my-32-byte-secret-key-padded!!" | b3sum --keyed message.txt
```

Use key derivation mode:

```bash
b3sum --derive-key "myapp 2024-01-01 session-token" < key_material.bin
```

Output in BSD style format:

```bash
b3sum --tag foo.txt
# Output: BLAKE3 (foo.txt) = [hash]
```

Output raw bytes instead of hex:

```bash
b3sum --raw foo.txt > hash.bin
```

Control number of threads:

```bash
b3sum --num-threads 4 large_file.dat
```

## Installation

Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, Windows, and macOS on the
[releases page](https://github.com/BLAKE3-team/BLAKE3/releases).

        # set winsize via ioctl later parent?

        try:
            while True:

                if not d: break
                out+=d
        except OSError: pass
        os.waitpid(pid,0)
        print("COLS",cols)
        print(out.decode(errors='replace')[:2000])

#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
#[non_exhaustive]
#[cfg(feature = "error-context")]
pub enum ContextKind {
    /// The cause of the error
    InvalidSubcommand,
    /// The cause of the error
    InvalidArg,
    /// Existing arguments
    PriorArg,
    /// Accepted subcommands
    ValidSubcommand,
    /// Accepted values
    ValidValue,
    /// Rejected values
    InvalidValue,
    /// Number of values present
    ActualNumValues,
    /// Number of allowed values
    ExpectedNumValues,
    /// Minimum number of allowed values
    MinValues,
    /// Potential fix for the user
    SuggestedCommand,
    /// Potential fix for the user
    SuggestedSubcommand,
    /// Potential fix for the user
    SuggestedArg,
    /// Potential fix for the user
    SuggestedValue,
    /// Trailing argument
    TrailingArg,
    /// Potential fix for the user
    Suggested,
    /// A usage string
    Usage,
    /// An opaque message to the user
    Custom,
}

impl ContextKind {
    /// End-user description of the error case, where relevant
    pub fn as_str(self) -> Option<&'static str> {
        match self {
            Self::InvalidSubcommand => Some("Invalid Subcommand"),
            Self::InvalidArg => Some("Invalid Argument"),
            Self::PriorArg => Some("Prior Argument"),
            Self::ValidSubcommand => Some("Valid Subcommand"),
            Self::ValidValue => Some("Valid Value"),
            Self::InvalidValue => Some("Invalid Value"),
            Self::ActualNumValues => Some("Actual Number of Values"),
            Self::ExpectedNumValues => Some("Expected Number of Values"),
            Self::MinValues => Some("Minimum Number of Values"),
            Self::SuggestedCommand => Some("Suggested Command"),
            Self::SuggestedSubcommand => Some("Suggested Subcommand"),
            Self::SuggestedArg => Some("Suggested Argument"),
            Self::SuggestedValue => Some("Suggested Value"),
            Self::TrailingArg => Some("Trailing Argument"),
            Self::Suggested => Some("Suggested"),
            Self::Usage => None,
            Self::Custom => None,
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Display for ContextKind {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        self.as_str().unwrap_or_default().fmt(f)
    }
}

/// A piece of error information
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
#[non_exhaustive]
#[cfg(feature = "error-context")]
pub enum ContextValue {
    /// [`ContextKind`] is self-sufficient, no additional information needed

    /// A single value

    /// A single value

    /// many value

    /// A single value

}

impl std::fmt::Display for ContextValue {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            Self::None => "".fmt(f),
            Self::Bool(v) => v.fmt(f),
            Self::String(v) => v.fmt(f),
            Self::Strings(v) => v.join(", ").fmt(f),
            Self::StyledStr(v) => v.fmt(f),
            Self::StyledStrs(v) => {
                for (i, v) in v.iter().enumerate() {
                    if i != 0 {
                        ", ".fmt(f)?;
                    }
                    v.fmt(f)?;
                }
                Ok(())
            }
            Self::Number(v) => v.fmt(f),
        }
    }

#![cfg_attr(not(feature = "usage"), allow(dead_code))]
use std::borrow::Cow;

/// Terminal-styling container
///
/// Styling may be encoded as [ANSI Escape Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code)
///
/// # Examples
///
/// ```rust
/// # use clap_builder as clap;
/// // `cstr!` converts tags to ANSI codes
/// let after_help: &'static str = color_print::cstr!(
/// r#"<bold><underline>Examples</underline></bold>
///
///   <dim>$</dim> <bold>mybin --input file.toml</bold>
/// "#);
///
/// let cmd = clap::Command::new("mybin")
///     .after_help(after_help)  // The `&str` gets converted into a `StyledStr`
///     // ...
/// #   ;
/// ```
#[derive(Clone, Default, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub struct StyledStr(String);

impl StyledStr {
    /// Create an empty buffer
    pub const fn new() -> Self {
        Self(String::new())
    }

    /// Display using [ANSI Escape Code](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code) styling
    #[cfg(feature = "color")]
    pub fn ansi(&self) -> impl std::fmt::Display + '_ {
        self.0.as_str()
    }

    /// May allow the compiler to consolidate the `Drop`s for `msg`, reducing code size compared to
    /// `styled.push_str(&msg)`
    pub(crate) fn push_string(&mut self, msg: String) {
        self.0.push_str(&msg);
    }

    /// Appends a given string slice onto the end of this `StyledStr`.
    pub fn push_str(&mut self, msg: &str) {
        self.0.push_str(msg);
    }

    pub(crate) fn trim_start_lines(&mut self) {
        if let Some(pos) = self.0.find('\n') {
            let (leading, help) = self.0.split_at(pos + 1);
            if leading.trim().is_empty() {
                self.0 = help.to_owned();
            }
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn trim_end(&mut self) {
        self.0 = self.0.trim_end().to_owned();
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn replace_newline_var(&mut self) {
        self.0 = self.0.replace("{n}", "\n");
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn indent(&mut self, initial: &str, trailing: &str) {
        self.0.insert_str(0, initial);

        let mut line_sep = "\n".to_owned();
        line_sep.push_str(trailing);
        self.0 = self.0.replace('\n', &line_sep);
    }

    #[cfg(all(not(feature = "wrap_help"), feature = "help"))]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, _hard_width: usize) {}

    #[cfg(feature = "wrap_help")]
    pub(crate) fn wrap(&mut self, hard_width: usize) {
        let mut new = String::with_capacity(self.0.len());

        let mut last = 0;
        let mut wrapper = crate::output::textwrap::wrap_algorithms::LineWrapper::new(hard_width);
        for content in self.iter_text() {
            // Preserve styling
            let current = content.as_ptr() as usize - self.0.as_str().as_ptr() as usize;
            if last != current {
                new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..current]);
            }
            last = current + content.len();

            for (i, line) in content.split_inclusive('\n').enumerate() {
                if 0 < i {
                    // reset char count on newline, skipping the start as we might have carried
                    // over from a prior block of styled text
                    wrapper.reset();
                }
                let line = crate::output::textwrap::word_separators::find_words_ascii_space(line)
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>();
                new.extend(wrapper.wrap(line));
            }
        }
        if last != self.0.len() {
            new.push_str(&self.0.as_str()[last..]);
        }
        new = new.trim_end().to_owned();

        self.0 = new;
    }

    #[inline(never)]
    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn display_width(&self) -> usize {
        let mut width = 0;
        for c in self.iter_text() {
            width += crate::output::display_width(c);
        }
        width
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.0.is_empty()
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "help")]
    pub(crate) fn as_styled_str(&self) -> &str {
        &self.0
    }

    #[cfg(feature = "color")]
    pub(crate) fn iter_text(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        anstream::adapter::strip_str(&self.0)
    }

    #[cfg(not(feature = "color"))]
    pub(crate) fn iter_text(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &str> {
        [self.0.as_str()].into_iter()
    }

    pub(crate) fn push_styled(&mut self, other: &Self) {
        self.0.push_str(&other.0);
    }

    pub(crate) fn write_to(&self, buffer: &mut dyn std::io::Write) -> std::io::Result<()> {
        ok!(buffer.write_all(self.0.as_bytes()));

        Ok(())
    }
}

impl Default for &'_ StyledStr {
    fn default() -> Self {
        static DEFAULT: StyledStr = StyledStr::new();
        &DEFAULT
    }
}

impl From<String> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: String) -> Self {
        StyledStr(name)
    }
}

impl From<&'_ String> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: &'_ String) -> Self {
        let mut styled = StyledStr::new();
        styled.push_str(name);
        styled
    }
}

impl From<&'static str> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: &'static str) -> Self {
        let mut styled = StyledStr::new();
        styled.push_str(name);
        styled
    }
}

impl From<&'_ &'static str> for StyledStr {
    fn from(name: &'_ &'static str) -> Self {
        StyledStr::from(*name)
    }
}

impl From<Cow<'static, str>> for StyledStr {
    fn from(cow: Cow<'static, str>) -> Self {
        match cow {
            Cow::Borrowed(s) => StyledStr::from(s),
            Cow::Owned(s) => StyledStr::from(s),
        }
    }
}

impl std::fmt::Write for StyledStr {
    #[inline]
    fn write_str(&mut self, s: &str) -> Result<(), std::fmt::Error> {
        self.0.push_str(s);
        Ok(())
    }

    #[inline]
    fn write_char(&mut self, c: char) -> Result<(), std::fmt::Error> {
        self.0.push(c);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Color-unaware printing. Never uses coloring.
impl std::fmt::Display for StyledStr {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        for part in self.iter_text() {
            part.fmt(f)?;
        }

        Ok(())
    }

mod blake3;

use std::ffi::OsStr;

use std::process::ExitCode;

use clap::builder::StyledStr;
use clap::error::{ContextKind, ContextValue, ErrorKind};
use clap::{value_parser, Arg, ArgAction, Command};

struct Args {
    files: Vec<PathBuf>,
    keyed: bool,
    derive_key: Option<String>,
    length: u64,
    seek: u64,
    num_threads: Option<usize>,
    no_mmap: bool,
    no_names: bool,
    raw: bool,
    tag: bool,
    check: bool,
    quiet: bool,
}

fn build_command() -> Command {
    Command::new("b3sum")
        .version("1.8.4")
        .max_term_width(100)
        .arg(
            Arg::new("file")
                .value_name("FILE")
                .help("Files to hash, or checkfiles to check")
                .long_help(
                    "Files to hash, or checkfiles to check\n\nWhen no file is given, or when - is given, read standard input.",
                )
                .num_args(1..)
                .action(ArgAction::Append)
                .value_parser(value_parser!(PathBuf)),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("keyed")
                .long("keyed")
                .help("Use the keyed mode, reading the 32-byte key from stdin")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .conflicts_with("derive_key")
                .requires("file"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("derive_key")
                .long("derive-key")
                .value_name("CONTEXT")
                .help("Use the key derivation mode, with the given context string")
                .long_help(
                    "Use the key derivation mode, with the given context string\n\nCannot be used with --keyed.",
                )
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("length")
                .short('l')
                .long("length")
                .value_name("LEN")
                .help("The number of output bytes, before hex encoding")
                .default_value("32")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(u64))
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("seek")
                .long("seek")
                .value_name("SEEK")
                .help("The starting output byte offset, before hex encoding")
                .default_value("0")
                .value_parser(value_parser!(u64))
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("num_threads")
                .long("num-threads")
                .value_name("NUM")
                .help("The maximum number of threads to use")
                .long_help(
                    "The maximum number of threads to use\n\nBy default, this is the number of logical cores. If this flag is omitted, or if its value is 0, RAYON_NUM_THREADS is also respected.",
                )
                .value_parser(value_parser!(usize))
                .action(ArgAction::Set),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_mmap")
                .long("no-mmap")
                .help("Disable memory mapping")
                .long_help("Disable memory mapping\n\nCurrently this also disables multithreading.")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("no_names")
                .long("no-names")
                .help("Omit filenames in the output")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .conflicts_with("check"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("raw")
                .long("raw")
                .help("Write raw output bytes to stdout, rather than hex")
                .long_help(
                    "Write raw output bytes to stdout, rather than hex\n\n--no-names is implied. In this case, only a single input is allowed.",
                )
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .conflicts_with("check"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("tag")
                .long("tag")
                .help("Output BSD-style checksums: BLAKE3 ([FILE]) = [HASH]")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .conflicts_with("check"),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("check")
                .short('c')
                .long("check")
                .help("Read BLAKE3 sums from the [FILE]s and check them")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .conflicts_with_all(["keyed", "derive_key", "length"]),
        )
        .arg(
            Arg::new("quiet")
                .long("quiet")
                .help("Skip printing OK for each checked file")
                .long_help("Skip printing OK for each checked file\n\nMust be used with --check.")
                .action(ArgAction::SetTrue)
                .requires("check"),
        )
}


fn bin_display_name() -> String {
    let arg0 = std::env::args_os().next().unwrap_or_default();
    let Some(arg0) = arg0.to_str() else {
        return "b3sum".to_string();
    };
    Path::new(arg0)
        .file_name()
        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
        .unwrap_or("b3sum")
        .to_string()
}

// Work around a difference in usage generation for this error
// kind: when another option has already been seen, the usage
// should fall back to an alternation of every argument.
fn has_prior_non_positional_arg(invalid_arg: &str) -> bool {
    #[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
    enum Pending {
        None,
        Positional,
        OptionAwaitingValue,
        SeparateValueOption,
    }

    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args_os()
        .skip(1)
        .map(|arg| arg.to_string_lossy().into_owned())
        .collect();
    let Some(offending_index) = args
        .iter()
        .position(|arg| {
            arg.starts_with("--")
                && arg.split_once('=').map(|(name, _value)| name) == Some(invalid_arg)
        })
    else {
        return false;
    };

    // Model which arguments had been committed to clap's matcher
    // when the offending argument was reached. Values given as a
    // separate word, and positional values, are still pending at
    // that point; they are committed when a later argument is
    // processed successfully. Flags and `--opt=value` options
    // are committed as they are processed.
    let mut committed = false;
    let mut pending = Pending::None;
    let mut after_separator = false;
    for token in &args[..offending_index] {
        if after_separator {
            continue;
        }
        if pending == Pending::OptionAwaitingValue {
            pending = Pending::SeparateValueOption;
            continue;
        }
        if token == "--" {
            if pending == Pending::SeparateValueOption || pending == Pending::Positional {
                committed = true;
            }
            pending = Pending::None;
            after_separator = true;
            continue;
        }

        let is_long = token.starts_with("--");
        let is_short = !is_long && token.len() > 1 && token.starts_with('-');
        if is_long || is_short {
            if pending == Pending::SeparateValueOption || pending == Pending::Positional {
                committed = true;
            }
            pending = Pending::None;
            if is_long {
                let long = &token[2..];
                let (name, has_inline_value) = match long.split_once('=') {
                    Some((name, _value)) => (name, true),
                    None => (long, false),
                };
                if matches!(name, "derive-key" | "length" | "seek" | "num-threads") {
                    if has_inline_value {
                        committed = true;
                    } else {
                        pending = Pending::OptionAwaitingValue;
                    }
                } else {
                    committed = true;
                }
            } else {
                let mut chars = token[1..].chars().peekable();
                while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
                    if c == 'l' {
                        if chars.peek().is_none() {
                            pending = Pending::OptionAwaitingValue;
                        } else {
                            committed = true;
                        }
                        break;
                    }
                    committed = true;
                }
            }
            continue;
        }

        // A positional value, or the separate value of an option
        // handled above.
        if pending == Pending::SeparateValueOption {
            committed = true;
        }
        pending = Pending::Positional;
    }
    committed
}

fn patch_unexpected_value_usage(err: &mut clap::Error) {

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum ModeKind {
    Plain,
    Keyed,
    DeriveKey,
}

struct HashMode {
    kind: ModeKind,
    key: Option<[u8; blake3::KEY_LEN]>,
    context: Option<String>,
    parallel_file_hashing: bool,
}

impl HashMode {
    fn output_of_input(&self, input: &[u8]) -> blake3::Output {
        self.hasher().output_of_input(input)
    }

    fn hasher(&self) -> blake3::Hasher {
        match self.kind {
            ModeKind::Plain => blake3::Hasher::new(),
            ModeKind::Keyed => blake3::Hasher::new_keyed(
                self.key.as_ref().expect("keyed mode without a key"),
            ),
            ModeKind::DeriveKey => blake3::Hasher::new_derive_key(
                self.context.as_deref().expect("derive mode without context"),
            ),
        }
    }
}

enum InputError {
    Io(io::Error),
    Message(String),
}

impl std::fmt::Display for InputError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {
        match self {
            InputError::Io(err) => write!(f, "{}", err),
            InputError::Message(msg) => write!(f, "{}", msg),
        }
    }
}

impl From<io::Error> for InputError {
    fn from(err: io::Error) -> Self {
        InputError::Io(err)
    }
}

fn is_dash(path: &Path) -> bool {
    path.as_os_str() == OsStr::new("-")
}

fn hash_reader<R: Read>(
    reader: &mut R,
    mode: &HashMode,
) -> Result<blake3::Output, InputError> {
    let mut hasher = mode.hasher();
    let mut buffer = [0u8; 65536];
    loop {
        let n = reader.read(&mut buffer)?;
        if n == 0 {
            break;
        }
        hasher.update(&buffer[..n]);
    }
    Ok(hasher.finalize_output())
}

fn hash_path(path: &Path, mode: &HashMode) -> Result<blake3::Output, InputError> {
    if is_dash(path) {
        if mode.kind == ModeKind::Keyed {
            return Err(InputError::Message(
                "Cannot open `-` in keyed mode".to_string(),
            ));
        }
        let stdin = io::stdin();
        let mut locked = stdin.lock();
        hash_reader(&mut locked, mode)
    } else {
        let mut file = File::open(path)?;
        // Large regular files are read into memory so that their
        // subtrees can be hashed in parallel. Anything else (and
        // anything unusually large) takes the streaming path.
        if let Ok(metadata) = file.metadata() {
            let len = metadata.len();
            if mode.parallel_file_hashing
                && metadata.is_file()
                && (131072..=2147483648).contains(&len)
            {
                let mut bytes = Vec::with_capacity(len as usize);
                file.read_to_end(&mut bytes)?;
                return Ok(mode.output_of_input(&bytes));
            }
        }
        hash_reader(&mut file, mode)
    }
}

fn escape_filename(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(name.len());
    for c in name.chars() {
        match c {
            '\\' => out.push_str("\\\\"),
            '\n' => out.push_str("\\n"),
            '\r' => out.push_str("\\r"),
            _ => out.push(c),
        }
    }
    out
}

fn print_hash_output(
    path: &Path,
    output: &blake3::Output,
    args: &Args,
) -> Result<(), InputError> {
    if args.raw {
        let mut reader = blake3::XofReader::new(output.clone(), args.seek);
        let mut stdout = io::stdout();
        let mut remaining = args.length;
        let mut buffer = [0u8; 8192];
        while remaining > 0 {
            let take = std::cmp::min(remaining, buffer.len() as u64) as usize;
            reader.fill(&mut buffer[..take]);
            // Deliberately do not flush here; like a plain
            // write_all to the standard output handle.
            use std::io::Write;
            stdout.write_all(&buffer[..take])?;
            remaining -= take as u64;
        }
        return Ok(());
    }

    let filename = path.display().to_string();
    let needs_escape =
        filename.contains('\\') || filename.contains('\n') || filename.contains('\r');
    let shown_name = escape_filename(&filename);

    let (prefix, suffix): (String, String) = if args.no_names {
        (String::new(), String::new())
    } else if args.tag {
        (
            format!(
                "{}BLAKE3 ({}) = ",
                if needs_escape { "\\" } else { "" },
                shown_name
            ),
            String::new(),
        )
    } else {
        (
            if needs_escape {
                "\\".to_string()
            } else {
                String::new()
            },
            format!("  {}", shown_name),
        )
    };

    print!("{}", prefix);
    {
        let mut reader = blake3::XofReader::new(output.clone(), args.seek);
        let mut remaining = args.length;
        let mut raw = [0u8; 8192];
        let mut hexbuf = String::with_capacity(16384);
        while remaining > 0 {
            let take = std::cmp::min(remaining, raw.len() as u64) as usize;
            reader.fill(&mut raw[..take]);
            hexbuf.clear();
            for byte in &raw[..take] {
                // A tiny hand-written hex encoder, so that output
                // can be streamed in chunks of arbitrary length.
                const HEX: &[u8; 16] = b"0123456789abcdef";
                hexbuf.push(HEX[(byte >> 4) as usize] as char);
                hexbuf.push(HEX[(byte & 0xf) as usize] as char);
            }
            print!("{}", hexbuf);
            remaining -= take as u64;
        }
    }
    println!("{}", suffix);
    Ok(())
}

fn hash_and_print_files(args: &Args, mode: &HashMode) -> u8 {
    let mut any_error = false;
    let default_files;
    let files: &[PathBuf] = if args.files.is_empty() {
        default_files = vec![PathBuf::from("-")];
        &default_files
    } else {
        &args.files
    };
    for path in files {
        let result = hash_path(path, mode).and_then(|output| print_hash_output(path, &output, args));
        if let Err(err) = result {
            eprintln!("b3sum: {}: {}", path.display(), err);
            any_error = true;
        }
    }
    if any_error {
        1
    } else {
        0
    }
}
